head: cloud/gguf-narrow-int-arrays
title: fix(gguf): decode 8- and 16-bit integer metadata arrays
body:
`GgufReader` skipped the bytes of metadata arrays whose item type is UINT8, INT8, UINT16 or INT16, but still stored the entry. The value was left default-constructed: the scalar `std::uint64_t{0}`, even though the entry's type said `kArray`. This had two effects:
- **Narrow integer arrays were unusable.** `qwen38_flash_next/config.cpp`'s `U64Array` says "Integer arrays of any width; GGUF writers pick the narrowest type", but it rejected these arrays because the value was not a vector.
- **An array key read back as a valid scalar 0.** `GetMetadataUint32` and `GetMetadataUint64` returned `0` instead of `nullopt`, so a mistyped key passed scalar checks silently.

Change: UINT8/UINT16 items are widened into `std::vector<std::uint64_t>`, and INT8/INT16 items, with their sign, into `std::vector<std::int64_t>`. This uses the same paths as the 32- and 64-bit types. Every item type is now decoded, so the skip branch is removed and the remaining unreachable `else` rejects the file instead of storing an array entry without values. The existing per-array bounds check and 128 MiB metadata budget still run first and are unchanged.

Test: `gguf_reader_test` adds `TestNarrowIntegerArrays`. It checks values at the edges of each width, including signed minimums, and that scalar getters return `nullopt` for an array. On unpatched main it terminates with `std::bad_variant_access`, because the stored value is the scalar.

Hardware validation: worth loading the supported model GGUFs once. A file whose loader currently tolerates a narrow array under a key it reads as a scalar would now see `nullopt` there instead of `0`.

Built in a cloud session (CPU only); Strix Halo validation pending.

> AI disclosure: I am not a software developer. Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) developed and tested this patch; this is not a claim of human developer review. Claude Code cloud session, CPU only, no GPU testing.

Test scope (Linux x86-64 cloud VM, no GPU, Ubuntu GCC/CMake rather than the Nix toolchain):
- `cmake --preset cpu-test && cmake --build --preset pr --parallel 4`: 54/54 hosted tests passed, including `gguf_reader_test`, `gguf_identity_test` and the Flash-Next/DS4 config tests.
- `gguf_reader_test` under `cpu-sanitizer` (ASan+UBSan): passed with no reports.
- `tools/ci/check-format.py` with the Nix-pinned clang-tools: PASS. `tools/ci/check-pr-title.py`: PASS.
- Not run: loading any real model GGUF.
